invariants: a browser action only reports durable acceptance or an authoritative work-order state and never directly paints the asset lifecycle as successful
requester, owner, approver, deadline, evidence requirement, reason and every transition are durable tenant-scoped facts
the requester cannot approve the same work order and only the assigned owner can start execution
completion atomically applies the optimistic asset lifecycle revision, immutable asset history, work-order history, minimum audit and governance outbox
compensation requires the completed asset revision and atomically restores the original lifecycle without deleting evidence
merge completion records a same-tenant target asset and never collapses identities in the browser
domain.compensation: disable the API flag for rollback; a completed order can use the explicit compensate transition when its resulting asset revision is still current

negative_tests: asset:read cannot create or transition work orders
cross-tenant asset and work-order IDs return no resource
stale asset or work-order revisions are rejected without side effects

stop_conditions: transaction latency or lock wait exceeds the approved budget, audit/outbox reconciliation diverges, or active-order conflicts grow

tests: G0 OpenAPI, feature contract, migration and generated-client lint
G1 state machine, validation, scope, idempotency, self-approval, evidence and optimistic-revision tests
G3 asset, history, work order, control request, audit and outbox reconciliation
G4 fixed-concurrency lifecycle command P50/P95/P99 and lock budget
G5 Windows Chrome create-progress-action-evidence journey with mock disabled
evidence: one trace_id binds each accepted HTTP response to work-order history, audit and governance outbox; completion also binds the resulting asset revision
